name: Poppy House
address: Poppy House, Kilmainham, Emo, Co. Laois
questions: Can you send a site map with the boundaries marked? How big is the site, does the lawn to the south-east of the house belong to it, and is the boundary fenced or walled all round, especially along the R422 (we have two dogs)?
Is there a floor plan or a room list with sizes? How big is the dual-aspect ground-floor bedroom, and how far is it from the shower room?

What heating system went in during the renovation (heat pump or other), what is the BER's kWh/m²/yr figure, when was the work finished, and are there certificates of compliance for the extension and the garden room?
Is water from the mains or a private well, and is drainage a septic tank or a treatment unit? How old is it, and was it upgraded in the renovation?
BuyerIQ flags radon as a critical finding for this Eircode: has a radon test been done or a sump fitted? And what is the building about 15 m to the north-west of the house?

ai.why: A charming, practically new stone house with a ground-floor bedroom, 10 minutes from Portarlington's trains and 15 from Portlaoise's ED, at €450k. But 117 m², three bedrooms and two bathrooms is small for six, and it sits on the R422 with a close neighbour.

electricity.detail: Likely connected; the listing says the renovation put in completely new wiring, but doesn't state the supply.

water.detail: Unknown; not stated. The listing mentions new plumbing only. Ask whether it is mains or a private well.

sewer.detail: Unknown; not stated, but a rural house on the R422 outside any village is almost certainly on a septic tank or treatment unit.

internet.detail: Unknown; the listing doesn't mention broadband and BuyerIQ shows 'no data' for this Eircode. The area falls within NBI's Laois rollout (Mountmellick and the Portlaoise deployment areas), so fibre is possible. Check nbi.ie by Eircode.
internet.speed: up to 500 Mb if NBI has reached it (unconfirmed)

groundFloorBedroom.detail: The listing places a 'dual-aspect ground floor bedroom' to the left of the entrance hall and a shower room off the rear hallway on the same floor; there is no floor plan, so its size isn't given.

type: Detached period stone house (two storey) with a single-storey kitchen extension
bedsNote: One double bedroom on the ground floor, two doubles upstairs; a separate garden room (office or studio) in the grounds
heating: New heating system fitted in the renovation; type not stated
tagline: A renovated period stone house of 117 m² with a contemporary kitchen extension, a ground-floor bedroom and a garden room, on the R422 in Kilmainham, about 3.5 km east of Mountmellick and 4.5 km west of Emo.

pros.detail: A dual-aspect double bedroom off the entrance hall and a shower room off the rear hall, so Gabor's parents need not use the stairs; room sizes aren't given.

Portarlington station is about 7 km straight-line: 19 weekday commuter trains to Heuston (about 1h05) plus InterCity services (the listing says under 40 minutes; Irish Rail gives a 46-minute average). The M7 is about 10 minutes.
Per the listing: new wiring, plumbing, heating, floors, kitchen and both bathrooms behind the original stone front; BER B1 (100–125 kWh/m²/yr band; exact figure not shown).

pros.text: Portlaoise ED with paediatrics about 15 minutes
pros.detail: Midland Regional Hospital Portlaoise is about 9 km straight-line; its ED takes children and opened a paediatric extension in May 2026.
About €3,846/m² for 117 m²; stamp duty about €4,500.

pros.text: Mountmellick's shops, GPs and schools 3.5 km away
pros.detail: SuperValu and the mixed Mountmellick Community School (706 pupils) are about 3.5–3.9 km west; The Rock NS (mixed) is 1.2 km and Emo Court about 5 km.

pros.text: Garden room for an office or studio
pros.detail: A separate glazed garden room with French doors in the grounds: a home office, or overflow space for a family of six.

pros.text: Private, south-facing rear garden; no flood zone
pros.detail: Mature trees shelter the rear garden, with a stone front wall and gravel drive; BuyerIQ lists no mapped flood zone, no mapped noise zone and no protected-area constraint at this address.

cons.text: Small for six: 117 m², three bedrooms
cons.detail: Below Alderfern's 125 m², which George called 'a bit small for all 6 of us'; with the parents downstairs the two boys would share one of the two upstairs doubles.

cons.text: Site size not stated; looks like about half an acre
cons.detail: Rough satellite estimate (2019 Esri imagery): about 0.15–0.25 ha (0.4–0.6 ac), depending on whether the lawn to the south-east is part of the site; well short of the 1-acre target.

cons.text: On the R422, with a close neighbour
cons.detail: The house sits roughly 15–20 m back from the R422 regional road behind trees, with another building about 15 m to the north-west and a tillage field across the road; it would need secure fencing for the dogs.

cons.text: Water, drainage, heating type and broadband not stated
cons.detail: The listing gives none of them; a septic tank or treatment unit is likely, and BuyerIQ has no broadband data for the Eircode.
BuyerIQ's one critical finding for this Eircode is in its radon category (detail behind a €39 paywall); its rough fix range for the findings is €800–2,000. Ask for a test.

cons.text: Not on the edge of Emo village
cons.detail: Daft's pin is in Kilmainham townland, about 4.5 km west of Emo and 3.5 km east of Mountmellick, so Mountmellick is the real local town.
The Rock NS is a DEIS Rural school with no report read; Mountmellick CS topped Laois in 2016–17 (95–100% to third level) but sent 56% in 2018, and no newer figure was found.

cons.text: No floor plan or room sizes
cons.detail: Daft has no floor plan and no MyHome copy was found; the bedroom, kitchen and garden-room sizes are unknown.
